summary: SIMPLE is the collective name for the IETF specifications covering instant messaging and presence over the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). This document is a guide to that large family. It sorts the specifications into categories, explains what each is for, and shows how they relate to one another.

plainLanguage.summary: There are lots of rule books for sending chat messages and showing who is online. This one is a map of the whole shelf, telling you which book does what.

subtitle: Guide to instant messaging and presence specifications for SIP.

tldr.problem: The IETF produced many related specifications for instant messaging and presence using SIP, making it unclear which specs do what and how they fit together.
tldr.mechanism: This document maps out the entire SIMPLE suite by categorizing specifications into presence and instant messaging areas, explaining each spec's purpose, and showing their relationships.
tldr.outcome: Developers and deployers can now understand the SIMPLE ecosystem and select the right specifications for their applications.

today: RFC 6914 is an Informational RFC that serves as a guide to the SIMPLE suite of specifications. The specifications it catalogs remain active Standards Track documents used by presence and instant messaging systems deployed over SIP.

sections.title: Introduction to SIMPLE
sections.content: The IETF has produced many specifications related to presence (knowing whether someone is online and available) and instant messaging (IM) using the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). Collectively, these are known as SIMPLE: SIP for Instant Messaging and Presence Leveraging Extensions. The specifications cover a broad range of topics, from the core protocols that handle subscriptions and notifications to the document formats that carry presence information to protocols for managing privacy preferences. The large number of specifications can make it difficult to understand what SIMPLE actually is, which specs make it up, what functionality it provides, and how the specs relate to each other. This document serves as a guide to the SIMPLE suite.
sections.plainLanguage: SIMPLE is a collection of rule books for chat and seeing who is online. This guide explains which books work together and what each one does.

sections.title: Presence: The Broader Picture
sections.content:
Presence and instant messaging are both part of SIMPLE but are well-separated and use different sets of specifications. A key part of the SIMPLE story is that presence is much broader than just IM; it enables communications using voice and video along with IM.

The SIMPLE presence specifications fall into several categories. Core protocol machinery provides the SIP extensions for subscriptions, notifications, and publications that form the foundation. Presence documents are XML documents that carry rich presence information, indicating not just whether a user is online but details like their mood, location, activities, and future availability. Privacy and policy documents let users express preferences about which information is shown to which watchers. Provisioning mechanisms let users manage their privacy policies, buddy lists, and other configuration. Optimizations improve the core machinery's performance, particularly on wireless links.
sections.plainLanguage: Presence means knowing if someone is available. You need rule books for how to ask, what information to send, what to hide from who, how to manage friend lists, and ways to send less information over slow connections.

sections.title: Instant Messaging: Two Modes
sections.content:
SIMPLE defines two modes of instant messaging. Page mode sends instant messages by including them in a SIP request; this is efficient for one or two message conversations. Session mode treats IM as a media type alongside audio and video, using an INVITE request to set up a session that includes IM. Session mode is more efficient for longer conversations since messages do not go through SIP servers. By treating IM as a media type, SIP features like third-party call control and forking become available for IM.

The Message Session Relay Protocol (MSRP) carries arbitrarily sized content of any kind between users, with the session set up by exchanging information in SIP and SDP signaling. IM in multi-user chat is supported using regular SIP conferencing mechanisms. Feature specifications provide familiar capabilities like is-typing indicators and delivery notifications.
sections.plainLanguage: You can send a chat message inside a SIP message if it is short, or set up a real conversation channel if you will send many messages. The channel way is better for long chats.

sections.title: Status Today
sections.content: RFC 6914 is an Informational document published in April 2013. It serves as a guide and overview to the SIMPLE suite and has not been obsoleted. The suite itself comprises many Standards Track RFCs that collectively define presence and instant messaging over SIP, with individual specifications for protocol machinery, document formats, privacy controls, and features available for deployment today.
sections.plainLanguage: This guide was published in 2013 and is still the reference for understanding all the SIMPLE specs that came before and after.
